factProposals.value: The SLO dashboard is served by a small standalone Node http server (dashboardServer.ts), not the MCP server or the Command Center's static Pages site - a third, separate live surface.
Nothing persists metrics across a process restart - MetricsCollector is in-memory only. The dashboard cannot and does not show 24h/7d/30d historical ranges; only a rolling recent-activity window.
The dashboard reads real DLQ depth from Redis (XLEN) when reachable, via an injected getDlqDepth provider - null, not a fabricated 0, when Redis isn't connected.

decisions.statement: Success rate and error budget use a rolling count-based window (default 50 requests), not an all-time average.
decisions.rationale: an all-time average would hide a currently-unhealthy system behind a long healthy history - exactly the 'metrics are inaccurate' failure path this story has to handle.

decisions.statement: The dashboard was rebuilt from a first flat-card pass into a structured enterprise layout (KPI summary, operational detail, needs-attention) after direct user feedback that the first version 'looks cheap.'
decisions.rationale: visual quality and information hierarchy matter for a page meant to be read at a glance by an operator, not just functional correctness.

decisions.statement: 'Error budget left' is clamped to a 0% floor for display, even though the underlying remaining value can go arbitrarily negative once breached.
decisions.rationale: found in review: a raw negative percentage (e.g. -173%) reads as a bug, not as 'badly over budget' - the CRITICAL badge and the red progress bar already communicate severity without a confusing number.

limitations.statement: The dashboard has only ever shown simulated job activity (runDashboard.ts's synthetic generator) and a simulated DLQ - it has never been pointed at Relay's real pipeline (queue.ts + callExternalApiAndPersist) processing real jobs, since nothing wires a running worker to this MetricsCollector yet.

No page without a <meta name="viewport"> tag was mobile-testable at all until this was found and fixed in review - without it, mobile browsers render at a 980px virtual viewport regardless of the physical screen width, so the responsive CSS never triggered.
